transcript: your calendar has Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. It does not have some day. That's the problem with plans like, I'll walk more. They name a goal, but leave the starting moment undecided. In a randomized workplace study, a reminder that prompted employees to write down a vaccination date and time increased flu shot uptake compared with a reminder alone. Not magic, just a more concrete plan. Psychologists call these implementation intentions, linking a specific situation to an action. Try this, when I put my lunch plate in the sink, I'll put on my shoes and walk around the block. The plate becomes the cue, not a negotiation about whether you feel inspired. Choose a cue you'll actually encounter, and an action you can realistically do. A plan won't create spare time or remove every obstacle. If circumstances change, adjust it. Don't just decide what you want. Decide what will tell you it's time to act.
normalization_note: Bilateral some day→someday normalization only; raw mismatch preserved.
